clue.text: Scotsman worn out?

parts.note: read as a Scottish surname (a 'Mac' man) that is worn when out of doors, this describes a raincoat named after its inventor

explanation.surface: A Scotsman looks exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn out' suggests tiredness, but read it as 'worn outside': the Scotsman is the Glasgow chemist Charles Macintosh, whose name went on to the waterproof coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The raincoat takes its name from a Scottish inventor, so a Scot's name is literally worn outdoors.

clue.text: Spotty is worthless

explanation.surface: Someone with spots is no good.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotty describes skin with the rash of a childhood illness; worthless means paltry or stingy, both senses of the same word.

clue.text: Sixth male bird reportedly had the bone

indicators.note: reportedly says the phrase before it is to be taken as it would be heard spoken

parts.note: a male bird is a cock; the one numbered six is cock six

explanation.surface: The sixth rooster, so they say, had the bone.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'cock six' sounds like the name of the small bone at the base of the spine.
explanation.definitionFit: The tailbone is the small triangular bone at the bottom of the human spine.

clue.text: At home clearly for an unlimited period

parts.note: being in means being at home
definitely means clearly, without doubt

explanation.surface: Staying at home, obviously, forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lasting indefinitely has no fixed end date.

clue.text: Attempt to include a shallow container

indicators.note: to include says the word for attempt takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Trying to fit a shallow dish in somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat, low-sided carrier for food or drinks is a classic shallow container.

clue.text: Too sure he's in trouble at the treasury

indicators.note: in trouble says the letters of the preceding words are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, the letters H, E, S

explanation.surface: An overconfident man is in difficulty at the Treasury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treasury' looks like the government department, but it is the definition in its general sense of a store of valuables.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasury is a place where valuables are kept, a warehouse or depository in a broad sense.

clue.text: Stream from the bay?

parts.note: a large bay supplies the first word of the warm Atlantic current named after the ... of Mexico

explanation.surface: Water flowing out of an inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Atlantic current comes out of the Gulf of Mexico; a large bay is the word that precedes 'Stream' in its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A large deep inlet of the sea is a bay, and it names the famous ocean current.

clue.text: Envoy lulu endlessly becoming unattractive

indicators.note: becoming says the letters change into a new form
endlessly says the word lulu loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A diplomat who is a real lulu turns out to be unappealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts LULU to LUL; 'becoming' rearranges ENVOY plus LUL. A lulu is slang for a remarkable person or thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlovely means plain or displeasing to look at.

clue.text: Confront and force concession when the cards cannot be seen

definitions.text: when the cards cannot be seen

explanation.surface: Staring down an opponent at the card table.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstare an opponent until they yield is one sense; a card lying with its value hidden against the table is the other.

clue.text: Principal cleric accepts company of another senior cleric

parts.note: arch means chief or principal, as in arch-enemy

indicators.note: accepts says the word for cleric takes another piece inside it

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric in a cathedral

explanation.surface: One leading churchman takes in a group from another clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: This Anglican office ranks just below a bishop, overseeing a part of a diocese.

clue.text: Bill trapped the Parisian man

indicators.note: trapped says the word for bill holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
le is French for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: An invoice caught out a man from Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name stands for any man in crossword convention.

clue.text: Experimental infant?

parts.note: a baby conceived through laboratory fertilisation, playfully described as the product of an experiment

explanation.surface: A baby used in a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A child conceived by in-vitro fertilisation is popularly named after laboratory glassware.

clue.text: Discontinue work with laity not available

parts.note: lay describes the laity, people who are not clergy
off means not available, as a dish on a menu

explanation.surface: Stopping church work because no lay volunteers can be found.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop working for a while, or to stop employing someone, is to cease work.

clue.text: Booked and given another drink?

explanation.surface: A booked guest is topped up again.
explanation.definitionFit: A booked table is held for you; read as re-served, it means served a second time.

clue.text: Claim remarkable green number first is cost-effective

indicators.note: first says the pieces for green and number come before the rest

parts.note: eco is a prefix meaning environmentally friendly, green

indicators.note: remarkable says the letters of claim are made into something different

explanation.surface: A claim that a striking green figure leads is about saving money.
explanation.definitionFit: Economical means thrifty, giving good value for what is spent.

clue.text: Particularly strong punch

parts.note: a blow that ends a boxing bout by leaving the opponent unable to rise

explanation.surface: A very hard hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing blow that floors an opponent for the count ends the fight.

clue.text: States posh fellow, unusually curt, had life-rent

parts.note: US is the United States
U means upper-class, posh

indicators.note: unusually says the word curt appears in an uncommon arrangement

explanation.surface: A grand American, oddly brusque, held property for life.
explanation.walkthrough: Life-rent is a Scots legal term for the right to use property, and enjoy its income, during one's lifetime.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are legal terms for the right to enjoy property belonging to another, without owning it.

clue.text: Lady, about 50, was without equal

indicators.note: about says the word for lady goes around the next piece

parts.note: a peeress is a titled lady
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A woman around fifty was unmatched.
explanation.definitionFit: Peerless means unrivalled, having no match.

clue.text: Dee wants fancy tart cooked with both sugar and vinegar

definitions.text: cooked with both sugar and vinegar

indicators.note: fancy says the letters are dressed up in a new order

parts.note: sour means tart or sharp in taste

explanation.surface: Dee would like an elaborate pie baked with sugar and vinegar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like a pastry but means sharp-tasting.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese-style sauce combines sweetness and sharpness from sugar and vinegar.

clue.text: Point frostily to Italian island

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
icily means frostily, coldly

explanation.surface: Pointing coldly at an island in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest Mediterranean island is a region of Italy.

clue.text: Definite finish

parts.note: the is the definite article
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: A conclusive ending.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the definite article plus a finish.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase marks the conclusion of a story or film, a final close.

clue.text: Said to be in favour of arm maybe, or front leg perhaps

indicators.note: Said to be says the word before is taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: for means in favour of
an arm is an example of a limb

explanation.surface: Support for an arm, or perhaps a front leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A forelimb is an animal's front leg or the equivalent such as a wing or flipper.

clue.text: Some citizen I then moved to the highest point

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A citizen says that he then moved to the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'moved to the highest point', with 'moved to' a link: the target is the highest point itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The point in the sky directly overhead is the peak, the topmost position.

clue.text: You are, it appears, in agreement in Germany about mountains in France

indicators.note: about says the German word goes around the other piece

parts.note: ja is German for yes, said in agreement

indicators.note: it appears says the two words are rendered as letters that sound like them, text-message style

parts.note: the words you are, rendered as the letters U and R

explanation.surface: Agreeing in Germany about French mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You are' is written as the letters U R, which sound like those words, as in text messaging.
explanation.definitionFit: The range runs along the French-Swiss border.

clue.text: Second-hand but still in service

explanation.surface: Something pre-owned yet still working.
explanation.definitionFit: Pre-owned goods are second-hand; something employed or in use is in service.

clue.text: Prosecution's case?

parts.note: case is read as a grammatical case, and the one suited to prosecutors is named from accusing

explanation.surface: The argument put by the prosecutor in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a legal argument, but it is a grammatical case: the one for direct objects is named as if from accusing.
explanation.definitionFit: This grammatical case marks a direct object and shares its root with accuse, which is what prosecutors do.

clue.text: Job to take someone to

explanation.surface: A job taking someone somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work; to take someone to task is to scold them.

clue.text: Prepared, ready by Lee seeing unclearly

indicators.note: Prepared says the letters that follow are made up into something new

explanation.surface: Lee has things prepared and ready, though his vision is blurred.
explanation.definitionFit: Having tired, watery eyes means one sees indistinctly.
